backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with the count variant (gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) so each bit holds the number of times that substructure occurs instead of a 0/1 presence flag. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits and leave the RandomForest settings unchanged. This is a one-line change to the featurizer.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Append the full RDKit descriptor vector (rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors, or the list in Descriptors._descList) to the Morgan fingerprint for each molecule. Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip extreme values to the 1st and 99th percentiles computed on the training fold. Fit the same RandomForest on the concatenated matrix. Physicochemical descriptors such as logP and TPSA are known to drive Caco-2 permeability.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Instead of the full descriptor list, build a compact vector of about 10 permeability-relevant features: Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, molecular weight, H-bond donor count, H-bond acceptor count, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, formal charge, fraction sp3 carbons, and number of acidic groups. Concatenate these with the Morgan fingerprint and train the RandomForest. Compact descriptors reduce noise relative to the full descriptor list.
backlog.title: Small curated physchem feature set

backlog.spec: Switch the fingerprint generator to the feature-invariant Morgan variant (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariants from rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), which groups atoms into pharmacophoric classes such as donor, acceptor, aromatic and halogen. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits. This gives a fingerprint that generalises better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: FCFP feature-Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan featurizer with an atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, count vector via GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Atom pairs encode topological distance between atoms and are less local than circular fingerprints, so they can capture chain length and polarity effects. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair fingerprints

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan featurizer with a topological torsion count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Torsion paths describe conformational flexibility, which relates to membrane permeation. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Topological torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the 167-bit MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) for each molecule and concatenate them with the Morgan fingerprint before fitting the RandomForest. MACCS keys encode curated functional-group presence that complements hashed circular bits.
backlog.title: MACCS keys appended

backlog.spec: Build the feature matrix by concatenating Morgan count fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 (each with 1024 bits), so the model sees local and wider environments at once. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged. The featurizer should loop over radii and hstack the results.
backlog.title: Multi-radius Morgan stack

backlog.spec: Swap the RandomForestRegressor for lightgbm.LGBMRegressor with objective='l1' (mean absolute error, matching the scoring metric), around 800 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, min_child_samples 10, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, and random_state=seed. Fit on the same Morgan features.
backlog.title: Replace RandomForest with LightGBM (MAE objective)

backlog.spec: Use catboost.CatBoostRegressor with loss_function='MAE', about 1000 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, and verbose=0. Train on the Morgan count features plus the compact physchem features. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are fairly robust on small tabular data of this size.
backlog.title: CatBoost with MAE loss

backlog.spec: Use xgboost.XGBRegressor with objective='reg:absoluteerror', max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.05, 600 estimators, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_weight 3 and random_state=seed. Fit on the Morgan features. The absolute-error objective optimises the median, which matches the MAE metric.
backlog.title: XGBoost with absolute-error objective

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) kernel matrix on binary Morgan fingerprints, K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) for count vectors or the equivalent bitwise form, and fit sklearn.svm.SVR with kernel='precomputed', C around 5 and epsilon 0.1. Predict on the test-to-train kernel. Tanimoto kernels are standard for molecular property prediction and often beat RBF on fingerprints.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Use kernel ridge regression with a precomputed Tanimoto kernel on Morgan fingerprints: solve (K + lambda I) alpha = y - mean(y) with lambda around 0.1 to 1, then predict with K_test @ alpha + mean(y). Centre the target on the training mean. This is a smooth similarity-based learner that complements tree models.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarity between test and training Morgan fingerprints and predict with a weighted average of the k=10 most similar training molecules, using weights equal to similarity raised to power 3. Fall back to the training mean when the best similarity is below 0.2. This nearest-neighbour model captures close analogues within the same chemical series.
backlog.title: Similarity-weighted kNN regressor

backlog.spec: Fit the existing RandomForest and a LightGBM model with objective='l1' on the same features, then return the average of their test predictions with equal weights. Averaging two different inductive biases typically reduces error more than tuning either alone.
backlog.title: Blend of RandomForest and gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Train three base learners on the same training fold: RandomForest on Morgan features, LightGBM with l1 objective on Morgan plus physchem features, and kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel. Return the unweighted mean of the three test predictions. Diverse model families reduce variance across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Three-model blend with RF, GBM and kernel

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, run an inner 3-fold split on the training data to get out-of-fold predictions from two or three base models (for example RandomForest and LightGBM). Choose non-negative blend weights that minimise MAE on those out-of-fold predictions using scipy.optimize.minimize on the simplex, then refit each base model on all training data and apply the weights to the test predictions.
backlog.title: Learned blend weights via inner CV

backlog.spec: Increase min_samples_leaf from 1 to 3 and set max_features to 'sqrt' so each split sees fewer features. Leave N_BITS, RADIUS and N_TREES unchanged. Larger leaves smooth predictions on noisy assay data and reduce overfitting to individual scaffolds.
backlog.title: Tune RandomForest leaf size and feature fraction

backlog.spec: Set max_depth to 12 on the RandomForestRegressor, keeping the other settings the same. A depth limit regularises the individual trees, which can reduce overfitting on a training set of only about 600 molecules.
backlog.title: Cap RandomForest tree depth

backlog.spec: Set max_samples=0.6 on the RandomForestRegressor so each tree sees a random 60 percent of the training rows, and keep bootstrap=True. Smaller per-tree samples increase diversity and can reduce variance on small, noisy datasets.
backlog.title: Bootstrap sample fraction for RandomForest

backlog.spec: Raise N_TREES from 300 to 1000 in the RandomForestRegressor. The loss is an average over many folds, so reducing the variance of the forest by using more trees is a safe gain, at the cost of a longer runtime that stays well under the 10 minute limit.
backlog.title: Increase number of trees to 1000

backlog.spec: Instead of the mean of the forest prediction, compute the prediction for each tree (iterate over model.estimators_ and call predict on the test features), then return the element-wise median across trees. The median matches the MAE objective better than the mean when the residual distribution is skewed.
backlog.title: Median of per-tree predictions

backlog.spec: Before fitting, clip train_y to the 1st and 99th percentiles of the training fold values, then fit the model on the clipped targets. Predictions are unchanged in form. This limits the leverage of a few extreme measurements on the fitted model while keeping the MAE metric on the original test labels.
backlog.title: Winsorise training targets

backlog.spec: First fit a Ridge regression on standardised compact physchem features (logP, TPSA, molecular weight, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds), then fit the RandomForest on Morgan features to the residuals of that linear model. At prediction time add the linear prediction back to the forest output. A simple physical trend is captured by the linear part and the forest models the rest.
backlog.title: Residual learning on a linear physchem baseline

backlog.spec: In LightGBM with objective='l1', set monotone_constraints so that the prediction is non-increasing in TPSA and hydrogen-bond donor count, and non-decreasing in Crippen logP up to the training range. Use the compact physchem features plus Morgan counts. Physically motivated constraints act as a regulariser for extrapolation to new scaffolds.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on physchem features

backlog.spec: Standardise the compact physchem features and the Morgan count features using training-fold means and standard deviations. Fit sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with hidden_layer_sizes (256, 64), alpha=1e-2 for L2 weight decay, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, max_iter 500, and random_state=seed. Scale the target by its training mean and standard deviation and invert the transform on output.
backlog.title: Standardised features with MLP and weight decay

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with objective='l1', learning_rate 0.01, 2500 trees, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 15, feature_fraction 0.4, and bagging_fraction 0.7 with bagging_freq 1. A smaller learning rate with more shrinkage usually gives a smoother ensemble that generalises better on small datasets.
backlog.title: LightGBM with slower learning rate and more trees

backlog.spec: Train five LightGBM models with objective='l1' on the same Morgan features, using random_state values derived from the seed argument (seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4) and varying bagging and feature_fraction. Return the mean of the five test predictions. Averaging over seeds reduces variance from subsampling without changing the model family.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged LightGBM ensemble

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, expand the training set by generating K=5 randomized (non-canonical) SMILES per training molecule with Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False), seeded from the seed argument (e.g. Chem.SetDefaultRandomSeed or by permuting atom order with random.Random(seed)). Compute atom-pair count features for each variant, stack them with the original rows and repeat the training targets K+1 times, then fit the same CatBoost model. For test molecules, predict on the canonical SMILES plus 4 randomized variants and average the predictions. This acts as a data-augmentation regulariser over SMILES representation. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES training augmentation

backlog.spec: Before fitting CatBoost, compute Tanimoto similarity among training molecules using Morgan bit vectors (radius 2). For each training molecule, count neighbours with similarity >= 0.5 (including itself) and set its sample weight to 1/sqrt(count), normalised so the mean weight is 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to CatBoostRegressor.fit. The aim is to stop densely populated chemical clusters from dominating the MAE objective, since the harness tests on unseen scaffolds. Leave features and hyperparameters unchanged.
backlog.title: Inverse local-density sample weights for scaffold-shift robustness

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, build a Tanimoto (MinMax) kernel on count-based atom-pair fingerprints, using a dense kernel matrix over the training set. Generate out-of-fold SVR predictions for the training rows with an inner 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed), and fit a full-training-set SVR to produce predictions for the test rows. Append this single column as an extra feature to the atom-pair plus descriptor matrix before fitting CatBoost. Out-of-fold generation is required so the CatBoost model does not learn from leaked in-sample SVR outputs.
backlog.title: Stacked out-of-fold kernel-SVR feature for CatBoost

backlog.spec: Change the CatBoostRegressor constructor to enable stochastic gradient Langevin boosting: set langevin=True, diffusion_temperature=1000 and keep loss_function='MAE', iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6. Langevin boosting injects calibrated noise into leaf updates, which acts as an implicit regulariser and an optimiser change rather than a different model family. Keep featurisation and the seed argument as they are. If the option errors, fall back to bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' with subsample=0.8 and report the failure rather than silently changing other settings.
backlog.title: Langevin (posterior-sampling) CatBoost boosting

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, carve out a random 15% of the training molecules (using seed) as an inner validation set. Fit CatBoost with MAE loss, iterations=3000, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6 and use_best_model=True with early_stopping_rounds=150 on that validation set, recording best_iteration_. Then refit a fresh CatBoost on all training rows for int(1.1*best_iteration_) iterations with the same seed and predict the test set. This replaces the fixed iteration count with a data-driven stopping point and a short learning-rate schedule.
backlog.title: Inner-validation early stopping with a refit schedule

backlog.spec: Keep the atom-pair plus descriptor features and MAE loss. Set CatBoostRegressor parameters rsm=0.5 (random subspace fraction per split), l2_leaf_reg=6, min_data_in_leaf=5 with grow_policy='Depthwise', and bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' with subsample=0.7, and set iterations=1500. Only these regularisation settings change. The purpose is to reduce overfitting to the many sparse atom-pair count columns, which should generalise better to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: CatBoost column and leaf regularisation

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train M=5 CatBoostRegressor models with MAE loss, each with random_seed=seed*100+m, and with bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' and subsample=0.8 so each member sees a different subset of training rows. Use iterations=800 per member to keep the total runtime within the 10-minute job limit. Average the five test predictions with equal weights and return the mean. This is a batch-level variance reduction that is cheap to implement and does not change the features.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged CatBoost ensemble with varied bootstraps

backlog.spec: Before fitting, replace the training targets with their normal-score ranks: compute r = rankdata(train_y)/(n+1), then y_t = scipy.stats.norm.ppf(r). Fit CatBoost with RMSE loss on y_t using the same features and hyperparameters. For predictions, map the test outputs back to the original scale by taking the predicted value p, computing q = norm.cdf(p), and returning np.quantile(train_y, q) via linear interpolation over the sorted training targets. This changes the target geometry and the loss the trees see, with no change to features.
backlog.title: Rank-preserving target transform with quantile back-mapping

backlog.spec: In featurize, keep only the atom-pair count columns that are non-zero in at least 5 training molecules, computed on the training split inside fit_predict (pass the kept column index to the test featurisation so the feature space matches). Replace the count values in the kept columns with log1p(count). Leave the six physchem descriptors untouched. Then fit the existing CatBoost model. This removes rare, noisy substructure columns and compresses the heavy-tailed count distribution, which is a data-side regularisation.
backlog.title: Sparse-bit pruning and log-count transform of atom-pair features

backlog.spec: After fitting CatBoost on the training molecules, compute its in-sample predictions and residuals on the training rows. For each test molecule, find the k=5 training molecules with highest Tanimoto similarity on atom-pair count fingerprints (MinMax similarity or Tanimoto on binary versions). Compute a similarity-weighted average of their residuals, with weights equal to similarity raised to the power 2, and add shrink * that average to the CatBoost prediction, with shrink=0.5. Use in-sample residuals only as a cheap approximation; if the correction hurts on validation, the shrink factor should be lowered. Keep all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour residual correction on top of CatBoost

incumbent.description: Implement rank-preserving target transform using normal scores to map the target distribution to a standard normal, then back-map the test predictions.

memo:
Incumbent is 0.3679 (mean_adjusted, 2 runs). It uses the rank-preserving normal-scores target transform (slot 35: 0.3698 and 0.3661, -0.0084 vs the previous incumbent). It sits on atom-pair count fingerprints with CatBoost (slot 21: 0.3763).

Helped: count-based features (slot 13: 0.3984), atom-pair counts (-0.0220), the target transform, and the Tanimoto-kernel SVR over the RF (0.4366 and 0.4257).

Did not help: CatBoost regularization (+0.0058), Langevin boosting (+0.0032), early stopping (+0.0015), LightGBM l1 (+0.0048), the CatBoost+RF blend (-0.0010), the median of per-tree predictions (+0.0028) and invariant Morgan (+0.0000). Doubling CatBoost iterations (-0.0022) is within noise (sd 0.0037).

Most failures were crashes from API errors (Descriptors import, fingerprint calls) or patch failures. Keep each SEARCH short and exact.

Next: a Tanimoto SVR or CatBoost blend on atom-pair counts with the transform. Also try atom-pair plus Morgan counts, and descriptors with correct imports and NaN handling. Tune SVR C and epsilon.
